outcome: No graph on n vertices exceeding floor(n/2) copies of each letter has been exhibited; the specific extremal question remains open, but Hefty, Horn, Muir & Owens (EJC 2024) and its 2026 JCTA follow-up 'Bottlenecks and bounds' advanced the surrounding theory of representation-number lower bounds (previously almost all work had been on upper bounds), moving understanding of the range of possible representation numbers without settling the floor(n/2) question itself.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks whether there exist graphs on n vertices whose representation number (minimum k such that the graph has a k-uniform representing word) exceeds floor(n/2). Both the live Wikipedia article on word-representable graphs and an EmergentMind topic summary (checked 2026-09-22) confirm this is still stated as an open problem: the highest known representation number remains floor(n/2), achieved by G_n, the crown graph H_{n,n} augmented with an all-adjacent (apex) vertex, giving 2n+1 vertices and representation number floor((2n+1)/2) = n = floor((2n+1)/2) — this construction is from Glen, Kitaev & Pyatkin (2018), which predates the 26 Jan 2024 frozen revision and is not a new development. The known general upper bound on representation number is roughly 2n (Hefty et al. 2024 sharpen this somewhat for non-complete graphs, e.g. 2(n-omega(G)) where omega is the clique number), leaving an unresolved gap between floor(n/2) and ~2n. Within the window, two papers by the same author group advanced the surrounding theory: (1) Hefty, Horn, Muir & Owens, 'Word-Representable Graphs: Orientations, Posets, and Bounds' (Electron. J. Combin. 31(4), #P4.2, published online October 2024, submitted Feb 2024) uses posets, Ramsey theory, finite geometry and probabilistic methods to settle several other open problems about word-representability and representation length for specific graph classes, and gives a general lower bound on representation number (roughly log|N(X)|/log(|X|+1) type bounds) for a finite graph; (2) its 2026 follow-up in J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 'Word-representation numbers of graphs: Bottlenecks and bounds,' whose own abstract states that 'most of the effort in this direction previously has focused on upper bounds' and that this paper 'provide[s] several lower bounds' instead. Neither paper is reported (in the abstract, any digested source, or the current Wikipedia/EmergentMind status pages) as exhibiting a graph whose representation number exceeds floor(n/2); rather, they develop general machinery for proving lower bounds on representation number for various graph families, which is progress on the broader landscape of the problem (understanding how representation numbers can grow) without resolving the specific extremal question asked in this bullet. I was unable to obtain clean extracted text from the EJC or JCTA PDFs themselves (repeated WebFetch attempts returned only PDF stream/font metadata, not readable body text), so my classification rests on the papers' own abstracts, on secondary digestions (Wikipedia's own article, EmergentMind), and on a Mozhui-Krishna 2025 arXiv paper on the related (but distinct, since it concerns a Glen-Kitaev-Pyatkin conjecture about bipartite graphs specifically, ceil((m+n)/4)) bipartite representation-number conjecture, which I did not rely on for this bullet's classification. No AI system of any kind is mentioned in any source consulted; all cited work uses standard combinatorial, poset-theoretic, Ramsey-theoretic and probabilistic methods.
competing_reading: The triage's `why` field asserted the 2024 EJC paper 'is reported to settle open problems on representation-number bounds' and that the 2026 JCTA paper 'addresses bottlenecks/bounds on this exact quantity,' which could be read as implying this specific floor(n/2) question was resolved. However, neither paper's abstract, nor any secondary source I found (including the live, current Wikipedia article on word-representable graphs, which still lists essentially this exact open problem), states that a graph exceeding floor(n/2) has been found. The 'open problems' the EJC 2024 abstract says it settles appear to be about existence and length of representations for particular graph classes (e.g. posets, cover graphs), not the general extremal floor(n/2) question. It remains conceivable that a lower-bound construction buried in either paper's body (which I could not extract as readable text) does exhibit a graph exceeding floor(n/2) for some specific n, which would upgrade this to `partial` or `resolved` with `resolution_direction: refuted`. I was not able to rule this out with full confidence given the PDF extraction failures.
what_would_settle_it: Readable full text (not just abstract/metadata) of Hefty-Horn-Muir-Owens EJC 2024 and JCTA 2026, specifically their theorem statements on general lower bounds for representation number, to confirm whether any explicit or existential construction is claimed to exceed floor(n/2) copies of each letter for some n. Also worth checking: any post-2024 update to the Wikipedia 'word-representable graph' article's open-problems section, and any survey talk slides by Hefty/Horn/Muir/Owens summarizing their results in plain prose.
